items.title: Cities of every culture build a real mix of house types
Every frontier town seats its wonder inside its wall ring
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Take the first 60 frontier towns, frontierSettlementSeedsNear(0, 0, 1500).slice(0, 60), and their plans, settlementPlan(getRealmDefinition(id)). In 15 of them the wonder stands 59 to 73 m from the centre, outside the wall ring (plan.wallRadius is 52):
- all six towns with the grid 'blocks' plan style (Suncoast and Clayborn, for example frontier_0_1 Fernstead);
- nine towns with the 'river' terrace style (Riverfolk and Reedfolk).
The tallest landmark then stands alone in the fields instead of dominating the core.

Required behaviour
For every one of those 60 towns, plan.named.get('wonder-1') is defined and its PlanSlot.radius is less than plan.wallRadius. (The 60 include at least one 'blocks' town and at least one 'river' town, and both styles must pass.)

Every existing plan invariant still holds, for all 60 towns:
- The wonder-1 parcel still holds the whole wonder: Math.min(plot.w, plot.d) of that parcel is at least Math.max(BUILDING_KIND_DEFS.wonder.w, BUILDING_KIND_DEFS.wonder.d) (10 m).
- plan.style is CULTURE_PLAN of the town's culture (getRealmDefinition(id).cultureId).
- plan.homes.length is at least 100.
- The wall ring keeps its towers and gates: among the keys of plan.named, exactly 2 start with 'gatehouse-', at least 4 start with 'watchtower-' and at least 30 start with 'wall-' (today these towns have 2, 5 to 12, and 38 to 48). 'keep-1' is present.
- The skyline rule: at least 40 of the 60 towns have wonder-1 radius < 48, and at least 55 have keep-1 radius < 35.

In every 'blocks' and 'river' town among the 60, no two parcels overlap and no street runs through a parcel:
- The parcels are every entry of plan.homes, plan.crafts, plan.market, plan.farm and plan.wells, plus the distinct values of plan.named (each a PlanSlot).
- A point p is inside parcel s shrunk by k when |dx*cos(r) - dz*sin(r)| < s.plot.w / 2 - k and |dx*sin(r) + dz*cos(r)| < s.plot.d / 2 - k, where dx = p.x - s.x, dz = p.z - s.z and r = s.rotation. A parcel's corners are its centre offset by (u*hw*cos(r) + v*hd*sin(r), -u*hw*sin(r) + v*hd*cos(r)) for u, v in {-1, 1}, with hw = plot.w / 2 and hd = plot.d / 2.
- Two parcels overlap when a corner of either is inside the other shrunk by 0.05. A pair of parcels that are both in the 'wall' district (s.district), where either has plot.w === 3 (a tower capping a curtain segment), may overlap.
- No point of any street in plan.streets (street.points) is inside any parcel with no shrink, the wonder-1 parcel included. Gatehouse parcels are exempt, since the main road runs through them.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing (plans stay deterministic, and the hamlet-to-city kind mix, docks where towns meet the river, the keep near the square and the saved-lot migration rules are unchanged).

items.title: Threats only land on targets within reach of the player
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Storms and other threats keep hitting Alder while the player is exploring far away. At 315 m from the saw bench the player got 'Storm at the saw bench in 1:08 · 315 m', with no way to get back in time.

Required behaviour
- Export THREAT_REACH = 90 (metres) from src/village/features/threats/threats.ts, the module that already exports stepThreats.
- stepThreats(slice, context, dt) never starts a threat, at dusk or at night, whose target is farther than THREAT_REACH from context.player (straight-line distance on x and z) when it starts. A target 89 m from the player can still be hit; one 91 m away cannot.
- If no target that suits a threat kind is within reach, that dusk or night passes without a threat.
- Near the player nothing else changes. Threats keep today's storyteller chances and kind rules: at dusk only storms (any target) and fires (a hearth target); at night only wolves and thieves (a store target). While a target that suits a kind is in reach, threats start as often as they do today.

The interface used: initThreats() returns the slice; slice.storyteller selects the storyteller (for example 'wild'); slice.active is null or the started threat with kind, targetId, x and z; context is { time, hour, day, player: { x, z }, targets, stock }; a ThreatTarget is { id, label, x, z, roofed, hearth, store }; FIRST_THREAT_AT is the earliest time a threat can start.

Concretely, with the 'wild' storyteller, one fresh stepThreats call (dt 1, slice.active cleared first) per day at the given hour, time = ((day - 1) * 24 + hour - 8) / 24 * DAY_SECONDS, days before FIRST_THREAT_AT skipped, and the three workshop targets kiln (-11, -4, hearth), store (-6, -5.7, store) and bench (-9, -2, not roofed):
- player at (0, 0), hour 17, days 1 to 20: at least 15 threats, every one a storm or a fire and within 90 m of the player;
- player at (0, 0), hour 21, days 1 to 30: at least 5 threats, every one wolves or thieves on 'store';
- player at (0, 330) at hours 17 and 21, or at (400, -250) at hour 21: no threat at all;
- with kiln (-11, -4, hearth) the only target in reach and the others 300 m away (store at (300, 0), an unroofed bench at (0, -300), an unroofed shed at (-212, 212)), player at (0, 0), days 1 to 30: at hour 17 at least 10 threats, every one on kiln; at hour 21 none;
- a lone unroofed target at (0, 0), hour 17, days 1 to 20: player at (0, 89) gets at least 15 threats; player at (0, 91) gets none.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing. If an existing test places the player out of reach of every target, you may move that test's player within reach, but do not weaken or delete any assertion.

items.title: Towns raised to a population house everyone (no campers packing the plaza)
The missing-axe favour stops misleading new players
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Rowan's lost-axe spot (the interaction point with id 'tool') is offered as a 'Rowan's lost axe · Help' target before the player has accepted the favour. The journal's 'Mark on the map' for a favour always leads to the favour's work spot, so a new player is sent to the axe spot, and tapping it there only gives a generic refusal until they happen to talk to Rowan.

Required behaviour
1. For a village state s, interactionPoints(s) does not include a point with id 'tool' while s.requests.tool is 'new'. It includes it once the favour is 'accepted', and no longer includes it once the axe is found (s.requestProgress.toolFound is true) or once the favour is 'ready' or 'complete' (as today).
2. Export requestDestination(s: VillageState, id: RequestId) from src/village/interactions.ts (the module that already exports interactionPoints). It returns, as a string destination id, where 'Mark on the map' should lead for that favour:
   - while the favour is 'new', 'ready' or 'complete': the workplace of the neighbour who offers it: tool -> 'timber' (Rowan), cart -> 'grain', garden -> 'mira', introduction -> 'workshop';
   - while it is 'accepted': where the work happens: tool -> 'tool', cart -> 'cart', garden -> 'garden', introduction -> 'gathering';
   - except that the accepted tool favour returns 'timber' once s.requestProgress.toolFound is true.
   The journal's 'Mark on the map' button for each favour leads to requestDestination(s, id).
3. The 'find' step keeps requiring an accepted favour: on a new game (s = createVillage()), actVillage(s, { type: 'request', requestId: 'tool', step: 'find' }) returns a state whose requestProgress.toolFound is false and whose requests.tool is 'new'.

The favour steps are unchanged: step 'accept' makes a favour 'accepted'; for the tool favour, 'find' sets requestProgress.toolFound, 'return' makes it 'ready' and 'claim' makes it 'complete'.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: The crosshair prefers targets the player can act on
items.brief:
What is wrong today
In the first minute, 'Old oak · Needs axe' steals the crosshair from 'Fallen timber · Collect', so the logs from Mira's first instruction can only be targeted by looking straight down. The crosshair should prefer the object the player can actually use.

Required behaviour
1. The exported type InteractionPoint (src/village/interactions.ts) gains an optional field blocked?: boolean.
2. Harvest targets are the points from interactionPoints(state) whose id starts with 'feature:harvest:'. Those whose action is 'Needs <tool>' (for example 'Needs axe' on a tree while the player has no axe) have blocked: true; every other harvest target has blocked unset or false. Once the player holds the tool (for example state.features.harvest.tools.stone_axe = 60), the same target is not blocked and its action no longer starts with 'Needs '. The action text itself does not change ('Needs axe' stays 'Needs axe').
3. Export targetScore(point: InteractionPoint, alignment: number, distance: number, current: boolean): number from src/village/interactions.ts. A higher score wins, and the in-game crosshair chooses among its candidate targets by this score. It keeps today's preferences (checked with an unblocked, non-resident point and current false unless stated):
   - better alignment wins: alignment .95 scores above .90 at distance 2;
   - at equal alignment the nearer point wins: distance 1 scores above distance 3 at alignment .9;
   - the current target (current true) and a resident point (point.resident true) each score a little above the same point without that.
   A blocked point loses to an unblocked point whose alignment is at most 0.1 worse at the same distance: blocked at .95 scores below unblocked at .86 (distance 2), and at distances 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5, blocked at 1, .95, .9, .85 and .9 scores below unblocked at .9, .85, .8, .75 and .9 respectively.
   A blocked point still gets a finite score above -10 (for example at alignment .8, distance 2, and at alignment .7, distance 4.5), so it can still be chosen when it is the only candidate.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Saving never loses the only legacy save, and autosave stops redoing work
items.brief:
What is wrong today
saveVillage(state, storage) has two faults.
1) Data loss. When storage is too full for the save to be written at all (setItem throws a quota error), saveVillage returns false, and a player migrating from an older save finds their legacy save keys ('alder.village.v3', 'alder.village.v3.backup', the v2 and v1 keys) gone afterwards. Their only save is lost.
2) Slow autosaves. With four grown cities each autosave takes about 93 ms, even when the stored primary is exactly the payload this session wrote last time.

Interface
saveVillage(state, storage?) and saveStorageFull() are the existing exports, with VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY (the primary) and VILLAGE_BACKUP_KEY (the backup). storage can be any Storage-like object (getItem, setItem, removeItem, key, length); a full store throws from setItem with an error whose name is 'QuotaExceededError'. The payload is the exact string saveVillage writes to VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY for a state. The legacy keys are 'alder.village.v3', 'alder.village.v3.backup', 'alder.village.v2', 'alder.village.v2.backup', 'alder.village.v1' and 'alder.village.v1.backup'.

Required behaviour
- Whenever saveVillage returns false, every legacy key that existed before the call is still present with its original value. For example, with a few hundred characters of legacy saves stored and a quota one character smaller than the new payload, nothing can be written: saveVillage returns false and every legacy value is intact.
- When the new payload fits on its own, saving still succeeds as today: saveVillage returns true, VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY holds the payload, and saveStorageFull() returns true when the backup had to be dropped (for example with a quota of 1.5 times the payload length and an 'alder.village.v3' key present).
- An ordinary save with enough space still leaves at most one of the six legacy keys, and saveStorageFull() returns false.
- After a successful save to a storage, if that storage's VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY value has not changed since, the next saveVillage call to that storage makes no call to JSON.parse at all (on the stored primary or on anything else). It still moves that previous primary into VILLAGE_BACKUP_KEY and writes the new payload to VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY.
- A corrupt primary is never copied into the backup. If something else replaced the stored primary after this session's save (for example with '{broken', with the payload's last character changed, or with only its first half), the next save still returns true, writes the new payload to VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY, and leaves VILLAGE_BACKUP_KEY holding something other than the corrupt string.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: A bread surplus speeds a town's growth a little
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Immigration into a town follows growthRate(s), its settlers-per-minute rate. A town sitting on a large bread surplus grows exactly as fast as one scraping by at its food reserve, so the town's economy barely matters to its pace. A reviewer asked for a food surplus to add a little.

Required behaviour
growthRate(s) rises with bread held above the town's food reserve (s.stock.bread compared with s.foodReserve). It depends only on the settlement passed in (s.population, s.foodReserve, s.stock.bread, the ledger of donations and withdrawals, and s.help).
- With no help, a town at or below its reserve grows at exactly today's rate, Math.max(GROWTH_FLOOR, Math.sqrt(s.population) / GROWTH_DIVISOR) (to 5 decimal places). For example: population 100 with reserve 75 and bread 0, 40 or 75; population 400 with reserve 300 and bread 300; population 1 with reserve 3 and bread 3, which gives GROWTH_FLOOR.
- The rate is always finite and never decreases as bread rises (for example across bread 0, 30, 75, 76, 110, 150, 225, 450 and 10000 at population 100, reserve 75).
- A town holding at least three times its reserve, however large the surplus, grows at least 10% and at most 50% faster than the same town at its reserve (with no help). For example population 100, reserve 75 with bread 225, 450 or 10000; population 400, reserve 300 with bread 900; population 64, reserve 48 with bread 144.
- The player-help bonus (today up to +75%, HELP_BONUS) still multiplies the whole rate on top. For example, at population 64 and reserve 48, with 400 timber donated (and nothing withdrawn, s.help 0) the rate is exactly 1.75 times the rate with no help, both at bread 48 and at bread 144.
- growthRate stays exported where it is, and GROWTH_FLOOR (.75), GROWTH_DIVISOR (12) and HELP_BONUS (.75) stay exported there with these values.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing, including the existing growth-rate, growth-pace and natural-growth tests.

items.title: Typed orders understand 'build a house'
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Typed orders to your own town misread the most natural phrasing. classifyOrder answers 'Which do you mean?' to all of these, even though the thing named is unambiguous and legal:
- 'build a house', 'build a well', 'build a lamp', 'build a shrine', 'build a storehouse'
- 'make a workshop', 'build homes', 'build a new cottage'
- 'build another house by the well'
'house' alone, or 'we need a house', is understood.

Required behaviour
classifyOrder(text, legal) returns { kind: 'order', order, confidence } with order.kind the named kind and confidence >= ORDER_CONFIDENCE (0.6) for each of these. Each LegalOrder in legal is { choiceId: kind, kind, label: kind }.
- With legal kinds house, lamp, well and stock: 'build a house' -> house, 'build a well' -> well, 'build a lamp' -> lamp, 'build homes' -> house, 'build a new cottage' -> house, 'build another house by the well' -> house.
- With legal kinds house, lamp, well, shrine, workshop, storehouse and stock: 'make a workshop' -> workshop, 'build a shrine' -> shrine, 'build a storehouse' -> storehouse.

Today's behaviour is kept for these cases (legal kinds house, lamp, well and stock):
- a verb with no named kind, 'build something', still asks back (kind 'ask');
- vague text, 'do something nice', still returns { kind: 'ask', prompt: 'Which do you mean?' } with exactly three options;
- mixed text, 'houses and lamps', still asks back;
- asking for a kind that is not legal, 'raise a town hall', still returns { kind: 'ask', prompt: 'We cannot do that just now. We could:' };
- words after 'by', 'near' or 'next' still name the anchor, not the order.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Morning letters carry only news since the previous morning, never repeats
items.brief:
What is wrong today
At every morning bell the game toasts up to two 'letters' drawn from the event logs. The same lines come back every morning whether or not they were already delivered, so 'Welcome to Alder. Mira's roof is waiting on timber…' arrives again every day. A line can also be toasted twice in the same morning (the founding-stake offer appears as its own toast and again as a letter).

Interface
For a village state s, toasts are the entries of s.moments with kind 'toast'; a toast's text is its line with the first letter capitalised, as today. Event lines are Alder's own s.events, and '<Town name>: <line>' for each line of a realm settlement's events (s.realm.settlements[id].events, with the name REALM_DEFS[id].name). The morning bell rings at 06:00; stepVillage advances the game.

Required behaviour
- A morning's letter toasts carry only event lines that appeared since the previous morning bell.
- Letters are still toasted at the morning bell itself, in the same simulation step as the bell banner: the single stepVillage tick that crosses 06:00 carries them.
- If nothing new happened, that morning pushes no letter toast. The bell banner and other features' own dawn moments are unaffected.
- A new event line added between two mornings (for example 'The storehouse reached tier 2.' appended to s.events) is toasted exactly once, on the next morning, and not on the morning after.
- No morning pushes two toasts with identical text.
- Letters keep today's selection: routine lines starting 'Collected ', 'Took ' or 'Stored ' are never letters; Alder's own lines come first, newest first, then other towns' lines with their name prefix; at most two letter toasts per morning.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing. If your change adds state that an existing test pins by its exact shape, you may extend that assertion to include the new field; do not weaken or delete any other assertion.

items.title: Buckets can be filled at wells, not only at the river
items.brief:
What is wrong today
An empty bucket fills only at the river. The bucket's fill step, actVillage(state, { type: 'feature', feature: 'wander', action: { type: 'bucket', step: 'fill' } }), refuses everywhere else with 'Fill it at the water's edge.', even when the player is standing right beside a well. Yet the player-built Well piece promises 'Water close to home; buckets for fires', and towns dig wells of their own.

Required behaviour
An empty bucket (state.features.wander.bucket === 'empty') becomes 'full' when the player (state.player x, z) stands within 2.4 m, measured horizontally, of the centre of any of these:
(a) a standing Well piece the player built: an entry of kind 'well' in state.features.building.pieces with condition > 0. Its centre is the centre of its cell: cell x + 0.5, cell z + 0.5.
(b) a completed well lot in any discovered realm settlement (any town in state.realm.settlements): a lot with buildingType 'well' and tier >= 1, centred at the lot's x, z.
(c) a completed well commission in the player's own town: an entry in state.features.claimTown.town.commissions with kind 'well' and complete true, centred at its x, z.

These do not count: a knocked-down well piece (condition 0), a well lot at tier 0, and a well commission that is not complete. Next to one of those, with no river in reach, the fill is refused and the bucket stays 'empty'.

Unchanged
- Filling at the river's edge works as before.
- Anywhere with no river and no counting well in reach, the fill is still refused and the bucket stays 'empty'.
- Taking a bucket from the store, pouring a full bucket, and a bucket's effect against fire all work as before.

items.title: Residents gossip about your escorts and caravan crates
items.brief:
What is wrong today
When the player escorts a caravan or has a crate commissioned, the caravans feature logs a caravan deed in state.features.caravans.deeds (entries { kind: 'escort' | 'commission', settlementId, at }). Residents never hear about it. No gossip deed appears in state.features.council.gossip.deeds, and no resident ever mentions trade or caravan work. Gossip has a 'trade' deed kind, and Nell cares about trade news more than anything, but no 'trade' deed is ever recorded.

Required behaviour
- Each new caravan deed for a realm town (its settlementId is a realm id such as 'willow' or 'cairn') becomes exactly one gossip deed in state.features.council.gossip.deeds within a second of simulated time. For example, after one stepVillage(state, 1.5) following the caravan deed being logged, the gossip deed is there. The same caravan deed is never turned into a second gossip deed, however long the game runs afterwards.
- That gossip deed has kind 'trade'. Its place is the town's display name: 'Willowbank' for 'willow', 'Cairnstead' for 'cairn'.
- The lines residents say about it, barkToPlayer(deed, npcId) and overheardLine(deed, speaker), contain that town's name. They contain no unfilled '{…}' slot and never the text 'undefined'.
- When such a fresh trade deed is the only news, pickGossip(state, state.features.council.gossip, 'nell') returns that deed.
- Caravan deeds already logged when the game was saved are not reported again after saveVillage then loadVillage, however long the loaded game runs. Gossip deeds recorded before the save are still there after the load, as today.

Unchanged
Every other kind of gossip deed, and the lines for those kinds, work as before. The existing council and gossip tests keep passing.

items.title: Settlers who want a home in their own style accept a piece-built home in that style
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Two authored settlers, Petrok (Clayborn) and Sefa (Suncoast), want 'a home in their own style'. In a player town of another culture neither can ever be satisfied. That stays true even after the player learns their culture's building style and builds them a home from pieces in it. Their verdict on such a home is the same as on the same home in the town's style, and 'style' is still the want they name.

Required behaviour
1. The PieceSite type gains an optional field culture?: CultureId. It is the culture style a piece-built place was built in.
2. The object returned by homeFacts(town, id, …) gains a field style: CultureId, the style the home is built in:
   - a piece-built home whose piece site has a culture: that culture;
   - a piece-built home whose site has no culture, and every commissioned house: the town's own culture (town.culture).
   When stepClaimTown(state, ctx) receives ctx.pieceSites and one of them is a house with a culture, homeFacts for that home (by the site's id) reports that culture as style.
3. In the running game (stepVillage), a home the player builds from pieces inside their town carries the style its pieces were placed in. Each placed piece records the building style that was selected when it was placed, as that culture's index in CULTURE_IDS. So homeFacts for that home's piece site in state.features.claimTown.town.pieceSites reports that culture as style. When a home's pieces are all in one style, that style is the home's. How a home of mixed styles is classed is up to you.
4. localVerdict(def, facts, town, …) treats a settler's 'style' want as met exactly when facts.style equals the settler's own culture (def.culture). So for a settler who wants 'style':
   - a home in the settler's own style: 'style' is not the returned want, and the score is higher than for the same home in any other style;
   - a home in another style, including the town's own style when that differs from the settler's culture: the returned want is 'style'.

Unchanged
Every other want and every other part of the verdict score work as before. Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Repairing damage and defending against threats earn standing and town help
items.brief:
What is wrong today
The reputation ladder has 'repaired' and 'rescued' deed kinds, each with an authored verdict and 12 growth help (state.realm.settlements[id].help). Nothing the player does against threats ever earns either one. Finishing a repair of storm damage, carrying home a bundle dropped by thieves, or standing guard until a threat passes records no deed with the town, and the town's growth help does not move. Only the flat state.reputation number goes up.

Required behaviour
This applies to threats and damage at the home village's own buildings, for example the village kiln or the communal store. Those count as realm 'alder'.
- Repair: the player finishes repairing damage with actVillage(state, { type: 'feature', feature: 'threats', action: { type: 'repair', damageId } }). A 'repaired' deed is recorded for 'alder'. Only the repair action that completes the repair counts. A repair action that leaves work still to do records nothing and gives no help.
- Dropped bundle: the player carries home a thieves' dropped bundle (damage with cause 'thieves', recovered with the same repair action). A 'rescued' deed is recorded for 'alder' instead.
- Guarded threat: a threat resolves because the player guarded it fully (its guard >= guardNeeded). A 'rescued' deed is recorded for 'alder'.
- Each such deed appears in state.features.reputation.standings.alder.deeds with realmId 'alder' and its kind. It raises state.realm.settlements.alder.help by 12.
- These record no deed and give no help: damage that residents mend on their own (self-repair), and a threat turned away only by lamps without the player guarding it fully.

Unchanged
Everything else the threats feature does on these events is unchanged: its moments, stock movements, the flat reputation bonus, the held count and the removal of finished damage. The existing threats tests keep passing.

items.title: A completed caravan escort earns standing and growth help with the caravan's town
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Escorting a realm merchant's caravan pays coins, but it earns no standing with the merchant's town and no growth help. The reputation ladder has a 'rescued' deed kind (worth 12 growth help in state.realm.settlements[id].help) for this kind of help, but an escort never records one.

Required behaviour
An escort completes when the escorted merchant reaches its destination with the player close enough and the escort pay is settled. That includes an arrival where the merchant's home town chest is empty and no coin is paid. When an escort completes, a 'rescued' deed is recorded for the caravan's home town, the escort's settlementId:
- state.features.reputation.standings[settlementId].deeds gains one 'rescued' entry with realmId equal to settlementId;
- state.realm.settlements[settlementId].help rises by 12;
- the destination town (the escort's partnerId) gets no deed.
These record no deed and give no help:
- a lapsed escort, where the player stays out of range until ESCORT_LAPSE runs out (the 'The escort lapsed' warning);
- an escort the player leaves with the caravans action { type: 'leave_escort' }.

Unchanged
- The coin pay: escortBonus(amount), taken from the home town's treasury and capped by what the treasury holds.
- state.features.caravans.stats.escorted and the 'escort' entry in state.features.caravans.deeds.
- The arrival moments. Once an escort completes, the most recent entry in state.moments is still the escort's reward moment (kind 'reward', chime 'celebrate'). Its detail is the pay line, or the line saying the town chest is empty ('…chest is empty…') when nothing was paid.
The existing caravans tests keep passing.

items.title: The morning comfort buff really makes gathering faster
items.brief:
What is wrong today
At dawn, owning a home grants a comfort buff with the moment 'A well-kept home settles you in a little faster today.'. selectComfortBuffActive(state) reports the buff: it is true while state.features.director.buffUntil > state.time. But gathering is no faster while the buff lasts:
- a hand gather, actVillage(state, { type: 'gather', resource }), is still refused if it comes less than 0.22 s after the previous gather;
- a harvest stroke on the same target (the 'harvest' feature's strike action) is still refused less than STRIKE_COOLDOWN (0.35 s) after the previous stroke.

Required behaviour
While selectComfortBuffActive(state) is true, both minimum gaps are 70% of normal: 0.154 s between gathers, and 0.245 s between strokes on the same target.
- A second gather 0.17 s after the previous one is accepted with the buff and refused without it. A gap of 0.23 s is accepted either way.
- A second stroke on the same target 0.26 s after the previous one lands with the buff and is refused without it. A gap of 0.36 s lands either way.
- Anything faster than 70% of normal is still refused, even with the buff: for example a gather 0.1 s or 0.14 s after the last, or a stroke 0.2 s after the last.
- An expired buff (buffUntil at or before state.time) changes nothing.
- The buff granted at dawn for owning a home is enough: straight after it is granted, a gather 0.17 s after the previous one is accepted.

Unchanged
STRIKE_COOLDOWN keeps its value of 0.35. Without the buff, gathering and harvesting behave exactly as today. The existing director, harvest and simulation tests keep passing.

items.title: Map overlay shows trade routes between towns
items.brief:
What is wrong today
The map overlay's links, historyMapLinks(state, townIds), show only two things: diplomatic stances between towns (pact, alliance, rivalry, dispute, embargo) and each town's internal supply chains. The owner asked for history to show on the map through 'map overlays for routes and alliances'. Trade routes between towns never appear, even between towns that trade all the time.

Required behaviour
- MapLink's kind gains 'route'. LINK_STYLE gains a 'route' entry with a non-empty stroke colour string and a width greater than 0, like the other entries.
- historyMapLinks(state, townIds) returns exactly one link of kind 'route' for every pair of towns where at least one of the two is in townIds, and either of these holds:
  - the pair has traded: their history relation, state.features.history.rel[pairKey(a, b)], has total > 0;
  - a merchant from one of them is on a trade trip to the other right now: a worker of a realm settlement in state.realm.settlements whose task.kind is 'trade' and whose task.partnerId is the other town.
- A route runs centre to centre: from and to are the two towns' centres, getRealmDefinition(id).center as [x, z], in either order.
- A route's label contains both towns' names (getRealmDefinition(id).name, for example 'Alder North', 'Willowbank', 'Cairnstead'). It also contains the relation's total traded as a number: 0 when the pair has no relation or has not traded yet.
- A pair gets at most one route, however many merchants are on the road between them in either direction, and whether or not it has also traded.
- A pair whose relation has a stance (anything other than 'none') already gets its stance link. It gets no route link as well.
- Pairs that have never traded and have no merchant on the road between them get no route.
- Pairs where neither town is in townIds get no route.
- Every link id in the result stays unique.

Unchanged
Stance links and supply-chain links are drawn as before. The existing history and village map tests keep passing.

items.title: Signature caravans count as trade for diplomacy and the chronicle
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Realm merchants now carry most goods between towns as signature loads (each culture's SIGNATURE_GOODS good), delivered into the partner town's signature store. The history feature does not count those deliveries as trade:
- they never raise a relation's traded or total;
- they never feed the diplomacy review;
- they never appear in any town's chronicle.
In one run with no ordinary trade, the three core towns exchanged 25 signature units in 45 minutes. Every relation's total stayed 0, and Alder–Willowbank drifted to -11.5 goodwill.

Required behaviour
- Each signature delivery from town A to town B adds its amount to the history relation between them, state.features.history.rel[pairKey(A, B)]. It raises traded and total by that same amount, at the same moment. The relation is created if it does not exist yet. Crediting may lag the delivery by a few seconds of simulated time, but never more than 10 s. Every delivered unit is credited exactly once.
- Outside a diplomacy review, a relation's total and traded always move together, by the same amount.
- The receiving town's chronicle, state.features.history.towns[B].entries, records the first signature delivery from each partner town as an entry of kind 'trade'. The entry's text:
  - contains the good's SIGNATURE_GOODS label word for word, whatever the amount (for example 'carved beams', even for a single beam);
  - names the sending town by its realm name, getRealmDefinition(A).name (for example 'Cairnstead').
- This holds in a game where nothing but signature caravans moves goods between towns, for example when every realm town's treasury is 0, over at least 45 simulated minutes.

Unchanged
Ordinary resource trade is credited and chronicled as before. The existing history, economy and caravans tests keep passing. A saved game still loads and carries on, and trade credited before the save is not credited again after the load.

items.title: Tier-3 milestone gates only ask for goods a merchant can actually bring
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Discovering one far-off town of a new culture walls every core town. For example, after the player discovers a Frostholm town about 2.7 km away, Alder North, Willowbank and Cairnstead all stall for good on 'Waiting for 3 Frostholm frost furs to raise the storehouse to tier 3.'. No merchant can ever bring those furs, because that Frostholm town is far outside signature-trade reach.

Signature-trade reach: two towns are within signature-trade reach of each other when their centres are at most 480 m apart (640 m for a pair with a pact or alliance) and the pair is not under embargo.

Required behaviour
- A town's tier-3 milestone gate bill may ask for a far culture's signature good only when a discovered settlement of that culture is within signature-trade reach of that town. The bill is what gateShortfall(town, lot) and stallReason(town) report for the town.
- A discovered culture with no settlement within that town's signature-trade reach is ignored for that town's bills, as if it had never been discovered. The bill asks for more of a nearby good instead.
- After the player discovers a Frostholm town more than 1.5 km from the core, no core town's gate shortfall ever lists 'frost_furs', and no core town's stallReason ever mentions 'Frostholm', over at least 40 simulated minutes.
- A reachable discovered culture still counts, as it does today. The Suncoast town frontier_0_1, about 330 m from the core, once discovered, still leads a core town's tier-3 bill to ask for 'sun_dye' within 40 simulated minutes, so gateShortfall lists it or stallReason mentions 'Suncoast'.

Unchanged
- gateRequirement(id, lotId, targetTier, cultures) returns what it does today when given an explicit list of cultures. For example, given ['frostholm'], some core tier-3 bill still asks for frost_furs.
- Tier-2 bills: every amount is 2, and they are the same with or without a culture list.
- Gates already paid stay paid.
- Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Resource amounts read correctly in the singular ('1 plank', not '1 planks')
items.brief:
What is wrong today
The 'plural with 1' bug was fixed only for signature goods. Resource amounts still read wrong in several places:
- threat repair needs, from bagText: 'It needs mending: 1 timber, 1 planks'. Tiles show as '1 tiles' or '2 tiles', where everywhere else the game calls them roof tiles.
- your town's building-site needs, from needsText: '1 planks'.
- filled orders, from goodLabel(good, amount): 'Order filled … 1 planks'. goodLabel('planks', 1) returns 'planks'.
- building-piece crafting refuses with 'Needs 1 planks.', and rebuilding a knocked-down piece refuses with 'Needs 1 planks to rebuild.'.

Required behaviour
- Export resourceAmount(amount: number, resource: ResourceId): string from src/village/content.ts. It returns the amount, a space, and the resource's display label in lower case. Planks and roof tiles are count nouns and take the singular for exactly one: '1 plank', '2 planks', '1 roof tile', '3 roof tiles'. Every other resource is a mass noun and does not change: '1 timber', '5 bread', '1 stone', '2 flour', '1 clay', '1 grain'.
- bagText(bag) and needsText(commission) write each amount this way. They keep their current resource order and separators. For example:
  - bagText({ timber: 1, planks: 1 }) === '1 timber, 1 plank'
  - bagText({ tiles: 2 }) === '2 roof tiles'
  - bagText({ tiles: 1 }) === '1 roof tile'
  - bagText({ tiles: 1, stone: 3 }) === '3 stone, 1 roof tile'
  - a house commission still owing one plank has a needsText containing '1 plank' and not '1 planks'.
- goodLabel(good, amount) uses the singular resource label when amount is 1, and the plural otherwise:
  - goodLabel('planks', 1) === 'plank' and goodLabel('planks', 2) === 'planks';
  - goodLabel('tiles', 1) === 'roof tile' and goodLabel('tiles', 4) === 'roof tiles';
  - goodLabel('timber', 1) === 'timber'.
  Signature goods still return signatureLabel(good, amount) for every amount.
- The building-piece refusals from reduceBuilding read:
  - 'Needs 1 plank.' when crafting a wall with only 1 of its 2 planks;
  - 'Needs 1 plank to rebuild.' when repairing a knocked-down wall with no planks.
  Any existing test pinned to the old '1 planks' wording is updated to the new wording.

Unchanged
The threats, claim-town, economy and building test suites pass.
